name: Jerzy Kulej
milestone_by_age_26: Won European Amateur Boxing Championship gold medal in the light-welterweight division at Moscow 1963 at age 23, followed by Olympic gold at Tokyo 1964 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Started boxing at age 15 in 1955 at the Start Częstochowa club, then joined Gwardia Warszawa. At 18, he was selected for Poland's national team under legendary coach Feliks Stamm, winning the first of eight Polish national titles in 1961 at age 21.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Częstochowa, Poland; father Mieczysław and mother Irena Pietrzak were of modest means in the Ostatni Grosz district.
primary_early_advantage_tags: state sports system, elite coaching, national team, early specialization
evidence_summary: Kulej emerged from a working-class family in Częstochowa to become the top amateur light-welterweight boxer of the 1960s, aided by Poland's state-sponsored sports pipeline and the coaching of Feliks Stamm. He started boxing at 15, joined the national team at 18, and won his first Polish title at 21 before claiming European gold at 23 and Olympic gold at 24. The state sports system and Stamm's coaching were the dominant early advantages; no family domain or financial advantages are documented.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Częstochowa, Poland in 1940; father Mieczysław and mother Irena were of modest means.
current_position: Died on July 13, 2012 at age 71 in Warsaw; final roles included Polish parliament member (2001-2005) and boxing commentator for Polsat Sport.

trajectory.event: Started boxing career at Start Częstochowa club.
Joined Poland's national boxing team under coach Feliks Stamm.
Won first of eight Polish national light-welterweight championships.
Won European Amateur Boxing Championship gold medal in Moscow.
Won Olympic gold medal in light-welterweight at Tokyo Olympics.
Defended Olympic title with second gold medal at Mexico City Olympics.
Elected to Polish parliament (Sejm) as member of Democratic Left Alliance.
Died on July 13, 2012 in Warsaw.

name: David J. Thouless
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD under Hans Bethe at Cornell in 1958 at age 24, but his Nobel Prize-winning work on topological phase transitions came in the 1970s-80s; no notable research breakthrough by age 26.

name: David Hockney
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from the Royal College of Art with a gold medal in 1962 at age 25, and was dubbed a rising star of the Pop Art movement after the Young Contemporaries exhibition in 1961.
early_history_summary: Hockney attended Bradford School of Art from age 16 to 20 (1953-1957), then completed two years of National Service as a conscientious objector working in a hospital. He enrolled at the Royal College of Art in London in 1959 at age 22, where he befriended R.B. Kitaj and emerged as a standout draftsman, winning the college's Gold Medal upon graduation in 1962.
family_context_summary: Born in Bradford, West Yorkshire, to a working-class but politically radical family; father Kenneth was an accountant's clerk and pacifist, mother Laura was a vegetarian and strict Methodist. Fourth of five children in a tight-knit family in a small terrace house.
parent_family_domain_summary: No direct art-world family background; however, parents arranged private calligraphy lessons from a Bradford School of Art tutor to encourage young David's artistic interests despite modest means.
primary_early_advantage_tags: RCA, Bradford Art School, Kitaj peer network, Pop Art wave, gold medal
evidence_summary: Hockney grew up in a working-class Bradford family with no art-world connections, but his parents supported his early interest by arranging private art lessons. He trained at Bradford School of Art from 16, then entered the prestigious Royal College of Art in 1959, where his friendship with R.B. Kitaj and exposure to the emerging Pop Art movement catalyzed his rise. He won the RCA Gold Medal in 1962 and was labeled a rising star at the Young Contemporaries show, marking him as a major talent by age 25. The RCA peer network and the Swinging London cultural wave were the dominant early advantages.
starting_point: Born in 1937 in Bradford, Yorkshire to a working-class family; father Kenneth was an accountant's clerk and pacifist, mother Laura a shop assistant and strict Methodist, raising five children in a small terrace house.
current_position: One of the most celebrated living British artists; renowned for painting, printmaking, and digital art; estimated net worth in the tens of millions; resides in Normandy and Yorkshire.

trajectory.event: Enrolled at Bradford School of Art, beginning formal art training.
Enrolled at the Royal College of Art in London after two years of National Service.
Exhibited at Young Contemporaries, dubbed a rising star of the Pop Art movement.
Graduated from the Royal College of Art with a gold medal.
Won first prize at the John Moores Painting Exhibition in Liverpool.
Major retrospective exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

name: Franz West

name: Juan Giménez
milestone_by_age_26: Published his first professional comic story at age 16 in Argentine magazines Frontera, Misterix, and Hora Cero in 1959-1960.
early_history_summary: Born in Mendoza, Argentina, Giménez was a fanatical comics reader who drew constantly from childhood. His father, whose work caused the family to move every three years across Argentine provinces, gave him early drawing lessons. At 16, he produced his first complete published story 'El último disparo' (later titled 'Los dos amigos') in Río Cuarto, Córdoba, encouraged by friend and fellow artist Víctor Hugo Arias.
family_context_summary: Born in Mendoza, Argentina; father's work required the family to relocate every three years across Argentine provinces for 18 years. Father could draw and gave Juan his first drawing lessons. Family was of modest means.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father had some drawing ability and provided early informal drawing lessons, but was not a professional artist; father's profession involved frequent relocations across Argentina.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early publishing, self-taught drawing, Argentine comics scene, peer encouragement
evidence_summary: Giménez was a self-taught artist who began publishing professional comics at 16 in Argentine magazines, aided by early informal drawing lessons from his father and encouragement from fellow artist Víctor Hugo Arias. His family's frequent relocations exposed him to different parts of Argentina but provided no special art-world connections. He later studied industrial design and spent years in advertising before returning to comics full-time in his thirties, but his first professional publication at 16 is a verifiable early milestone. The dominant advantage was self-driven repetition and early entry into the Argentine comics publishing ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in 1943 in Mendoza, Argentina; father's work caused the family to relocate every three years across Argentine provinces; father had some drawing ability and gave early informal lessons.
current_position: Died on April 2, 2020 at age 76 in Mendoza, Argentina from COVID-19; final work included the Metabarons series and ongoing sci-fi comics.

trajectory.event: Published first professional comic story in Argentine magazines Frontera, Misterix, and Hora Cero.
Left South America and settled on the Spanish Costa Brava, returning to comics full-time.
Published Estrella Negra, his first color work, in Europe.
Began the Metabarons saga with Alejandro Jodorowsky for Les Humanoïdes Associés.
Completed the eighth and final Metabarons book.
Died on April 2, 2020 in Mendoza from COVID-19 complications.

name: John Williams
milestone_by_age_26: Composed his first feature film score for Daddy-O in 1958 at age 26, while working as a session pianist for major Hollywood composers including Henry Mancini, Alfred Newman, and Franz Waxman.
early_history_summary: Son of jazz drummer Johnny Williams, John Williams grew up in a musical household in Queens, NY, and moved to Los Angeles at 16. He studied at UCLA and LA City College, served in the US Air Force from 1951-1954, then studied piano at Juilliard with Rosina Lhévinne. After switching focus to composition, he returned to Los Angeles and began working as a studio pianist and orchestrator in 1956, leading to his first film score in 1958.
family_context_summary: Born in Flushing, Queens, to Esther and Johnny Williams, a jazz drummer and percussionist who played with the Raymond Scott Quintet and CBS radio orchestra. Family moved to Los Angeles in 1948 when Johnny sought studio work. Musical household with siblings who also became musicians.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a professional jazz drummer and studio percussionist in New York and Hollywood, providing direct immersion in the music profession. Father collaborated with Bernard Herrmann and worked in film studio orchestras, giving John early exposure to the film music world.
primary_early_advantage_tags: musician father, studio access, Hollywood ecosystem, Juilliard, orchestration training
evidence_summary: Williams grew up in a musical family where his father was a prominent jazz drummer and Hollywood studio percussionist, providing direct domain immersion and industry access from childhood. He studied piano and composition at UCLA, Juilliard, and privately with Mario Castelnuovo-Tedesco, building deep orchestration skills. By 26, he was a working session pianist for major film composers and had scored his first feature film. The father's music profession and Hollywood studio access were the dominant early advantages, supplemented by elite formal training.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Flushing, Queens, NY to a musical family; father Johnny Williams was a jazz drummer and CBS radio orchestra percussionist; family moved to Los Angeles in 1948 for father's studio work.
current_position: At age 93, still active as one of the most celebrated film composers in history with 5 Academy Awards and 54 nominations; conductor laureate of the Boston Pops; net worth estimated at $100-300 million.

trajectory.event: Served in US Air Force as pianist, bassist, and arranger for the Air Force Band.
Studied piano at Juilliard with Rosina Lhévinne, then switched focus to composition.
Composed his first feature film score for Daddy-O while working as a Hollywood session pianist.
First collaboration with Steven Spielberg on The Sugarland Express.
Composed the iconic score for Star Wars, winning an Academy Award.
Became conductor and music director of the Boston Pops Orchestra.
Composed score for Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, among his most widely recognized works.

name: Salvador Sánchez
milestone_by_age_26: Won the WBC and The Ring featherweight world championship by defeating Danny Lopez via 13th-round TKO on February 2, 1980 at age 21, and successfully defended it multiple times before his death at 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Santiago Tianguistenco, a small town in the State of Mexico, Sánchez was one of 11 children. He started boxing at 13 and turned professional at 16 in 1975 after only nine amateur bouts. He quickly piled up wins against tough Mexican opposition and moved up to featherweight, where he won the WBC world title at 21.
family_context_summary: Born to Felipe Sánchez and María Luisa Narváez in Santiago Tianguistenco, a small town (pop. 3,000) in the State of Mexico. One of 11 children; family was of modest means. His mother ran a beauty salon and his father initially opposed his boxing career.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family boxing background mentioned.
primary_early_advantage_tags: natural talent, early pro debut, Mexican boxing culture, small-town grit
evidence_summary: Sánchez emerged from a large, poor family in a small Mexican town to become WBC featherweight world champion at 21, widely regarded as one of the greatest featherweights ever. He started boxing at 13, turned pro at 16 after only nine amateur bouts, and defeated seasoned opponents with exceptional natural boxing ability, speed, and stamina. His manager Cristobal Rosas provided career guidance, but the dominant advantage was prodigy-level physical talent and early immersion in Mexico's deep boxing culture. He died at 23 in a car accident, cutting short a potentially legendary career.
starting_point: Born in 1959 in Santiago Tianguistenco, a small town in the State of Mexico; one of 11 children in a family of modest means; father Felipe and mother María Luisa.
current_position: Died on August 12, 1982 at age 23 in a car accident near Querétaro, Mexico; was the reigning WBC featherweight world champion at the time of death.

trajectory.event: Turned professional boxer after only nine amateur bouts.
Won WBC featherweight world championship by defeating Danny Lopez via 13th-round TKO on February 2.
Named Fighter of the Year by The Ring magazine alongside Sugar Ray Leonard.
Defeated Azumah Nelson in his final fight on July 21; died in a car crash on August 12.

name: Zurab Azmaiparashvili
milestone_by_age_26: Won the USSR Junior Chess Championship in 1978 at age 18, was European Junior vice-champion in 1980, and won the Georgian Championship in 1980 at age 20, followed by international tournament victories at Pavlodar 1982 by age 22.
early_history_summary: Born in Tbilisi, Georgian SSR, Azmaiparashvili was a chess prodigy who won the Georgian schoolboy championship in 1973 at age 13, joined the USSR youth games champion Georgian team in 1976, and won the USSR junior championship in 1978. He earned the International Master title in 1984 and Grandmaster title in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in Tbilisi, Georgian SSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet chess system, Georgian chess tradition, junior championships, Tbilisi chess culture
evidence_summary: Azmaiparashvili rose through the Soviet Union's elite chess pipeline, winning the Georgian schoolboy championship at 13 and the USSR junior championship at 18. The Soviet state chess system provided structured training, competitive opportunities, and access to strong players and coaches in Tbilisi, a city with deep chess tradition. He became International Master in 1984 and Grandmaster in 1988, later serving as trainer for Garry Kasparov. The dominant early advantage was immersion in the Soviet chess performance pipeline from a young age.
starting_point: Born in 1960 in Tbilisi, Georgian SSR, Soviet Union; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: President of the European Chess Union as of 2024; FIDE rating 2637; peak rating 2702 (2003); resides in Tbilisi, Georgia.

trajectory.event: Won Georgian schoolboy chess championship.
Won USSR Junior Chess Championship and earned USSR Master of Sport title.
Won Georgian Chess Championship and was European Junior vice-champion.
Won international tournament at Pavlodar.
Awarded the International Grandmaster title.
Won the European Individual Chess Championship in Silivri.
Became President of the European Chess Union.

name: Charles Leclerc
milestone_by_age_26: Won the GP3 Series championship in 2016 at age 19 and the FIA Formula 2 Championship in 2017 at age 20, then became a Ferrari F1 driver in 2019 with multiple Grand Prix wins by age 25.
early_history_summary: Born and raised in Monte Carlo, Monaco, Leclerc began karting at age 3.5 at a track owned by the father of his godfather, F1 driver Jules Bianchi. He won the junior World Cup in karting in 2011, then progressed through Formula Renault 2.0, FIA Formula 3, GP3 (champion 2016), and F2 (champion 2017) before joining F1 with Sauber in 2018 and Ferrari in 2019.
family_context_summary: Born in Monte Carlo, Monaco; father Hervé Leclerc was a Formula Three racing driver in the 1980s who later managed Charles's career. Mother Pascale was a hairdresser. Family was not particularly wealthy despite living in Monaco; Leclerc had to stop karting in 2011 due to lack of funds. Godfather was F1 driver Jules Bianchi. Paternal step-grandfather founded the Novares Group manufacturing company, which helped cover some costs.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a former Formula Three racing driver who introduced Charles to karting at age 3.5 and managed his early career, providing direct domain expertise and racing industry connections. Godfather Jules Bianchi was an F1 driver who mentored Charles and connected him to the Ferrari Driver Academy via Nicolas Todt.
primary_early_advantage_tags: racing driver father, karting from age 3, Bianchi mentorship, Ferrari Driver Academy, Monaco motorsport ecosystem, Nicolas Todt management
evidence_summary: Leclerc's early career was shaped by deep family-domain immersion: his father was a former F3 racer who introduced him to karting as a toddler, and his godfather Jules Bianchi was an F1 driver who mentored him and connected him to the Ferrari Driver Academy through manager Nicolas Todt. Despite financial constraints that briefly halted his karting in 2011, Leclerc's natural talent and the Bianchi-Todt-Ferrari network propelled him to GP3 and F2 championships by age 20. Growing up in Monaco, home of the most famous F1 race, provided unique geographic immersion in motorsport culture. The dominant advantages were family domain expertise and the elite motorsport network accessed through Bianchi and Todt.
starting_point: Born in 1997 in Monte Carlo, Monaco; father Hervé was a former Formula Three racing driver, mother Pascale a former hairdresser; family was not particularly wealthy despite Monaco address.
current_position: Ferrari Formula One driver since 2019; eight-time Grand Prix winner; 2022 World Championship runner-up; won 2024 Monaco Grand Prix; estimated net worth $50-100 million.

trajectory.event: Won junior World Cup in karting despite engine problems forcing him to start last.
Won the GP3 Series championship with ART Grand Prix.
Won the inaugural FIA Formula 2 Championship with Prema in rookie season.
Made Formula One debut with Sauber, scoring multiple points finishes.
Joined Ferrari, won maiden F1 races at Belgium and Italian Grands Prix.
Finished runner-up to Max Verstappen in the F1 World Drivers' Championship with three wins.
Won the Monaco Grand Prix, becoming the first Monégasque driver to win the race in 93 years.

name: Ruslana Korshunova
milestone_by_age_26: Hailed by British Vogue as 'a face to be excited about' in 2005 at age 18, appearing on covers of Elle France and Vogue Russia and in campaigns for Marc Jacobs, Christian Dior, and Vera Wang by age 19.
early_history_summary: Born in Uelkal, Chukotka, Russia, Korshunova moved to Almaty, Kazakhstan as a child. She was discovered at age 16 in November 2003 by Models 1 booker Debbie Jones, who spotted her photograph in a magazine article about a German language club in Almaty. Within two years, she was walking in New York Fashion Week and appearing on major magazine covers, represented by elite agencies including IMG and Marilyn Model Agency.
family_context_summary: Born in Uelkal, Chukotka, Russia; father Sergey Korshunov was a Red Army officer who died in 1992 when she was five. Mother Valentina Kutenkova raised her; family later moved to Almaty, Kazakhstan. She was enrolled in a school for gifted children and was fluent in four languages.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no family connections to fashion or modeling industry.
primary_early_advantage_tags: extraordinary beauty, agency discovery, international modeling, Vogue recognition, multilingual gifted child
evidence_summary: Korshunova's modeling career was launched by her extraordinary physical appearance, which caught the attention of a London agency booker through a magazine photograph when she was 16. Within two years, she was hailed by British Vogue and appeared on covers of Elle France and Vogue Russia, working with top designers and photographers. Her father, a Red Army officer, died when she was five, and the family was of modest means in Kazakhstan. The dominant advantage was prodigy-level physical appearance (extraordinary beauty) that triggered industry discovery, supplemented by the elite agency network that rapidly elevated her. She died at 20 in 2008.
starting_point: Born in 1987 in Uelkal, Chukotka, Russia; father Sergey was a Red Army officer who died when she was 5; mother Valentina raised her; family moved to Almaty, Kazakhstan; enrolled in a school for gifted children.
current_position: Died on June 28, 2008 at age 20 in an apparent suicide in New York City; was an internationally recognized fashion model at the time of death.

trajectory.event: Discovered by Models 1 booker Debbie Jones after being spotted in a magazine article about Almaty's German language club.
Hailed by British Vogue as 'a face to be excited about'; appeared on covers of Elle France and Vogue Russia.
Appeared in Vogue Italia feature 'Broken Dolls'; earning approximately $7,000 per shoot.
Died on June 28, 2008, in an apparent fall from her ninth-floor Manhattan apartment.

name: John Young
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from Georgia Tech with a BS in aeronautical engineering with highest honors in 1952 at age 22 and served as a Navy destroyer officer, but NASA astronaut selection came in 1962 at age 32; no material space-related milestone by age 26.
